articles.title: Nature Medicine Admits Science Has a Reproducibility Crisis — And the System Is Still Failing to Fix It
articles.summary: A landmark review in Nature Medicine confirms that reproducibility — the bedrock of trustworthy science — is not consistently implemented across biomedical research, with persistent barriers left unresolved despite years of awareness. This is the replication crisis in plain sight: the studies guiding clinical decisions, drug approvals, and public health policy cannot reliably be reproduced. The institutions profiting from this broken system have had every incentive to let it fester.

articles.title: Progesterone Suppressed as Depression Treatment While SSRIs Reign — Here's What the Research Actually Shows
articles.summary: Emerging research links chronic stress to measurable neurological disruption and points to progesterone as a plausible therapeutic intervention — a finding that has received virtually no mainstream clinical attention while SSRI prescriptions hit record highs. The psychiatric-pharmaceutical complex has systematically ignored hormonal and metabolic approaches to depression that cannot be patented and monetized. This research demands a reckoning with why cheap, bioidentical interventions are buried while billion-dollar pill franchises dominate treatment guidelines.

articles.title: SSRIs Show Immune Checkpoint Interaction in Cancer Patients — Data the Oncology Establishment Isn't Talking About
articles.summary: A target trial emulation published in PLOS Medicine finds that SSRI use among solid tumor patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors produces measurably different outcomes compared to benzodiazepine users — a finding with profound implications for both oncology and psychiatric prescribing. This intersection between psychiatric drug exposure and cancer immunotherapy has been almost entirely absent from clinical guidelines and mainstream oncology discourse. If SSRIs are modulating anti-tumor immunity, the millions of cancer patients on them deserve answers now.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Is at the Root of Cancer and Chronic Inflammation — And Metabolic Medicine Is Being Ignored
articles.summary: Research increasingly confirms that mitochondrial dysfunction drives both chronic inflammation and elevated cancer risk — a metabolic framework that challenges the somatic mutation theory dominating oncology research and funding for decades. While billions pour into genetic and immunological cancer treatments, the metabolic theory of cancer pioneered by researchers like Thomas Seyfried remains systematically underfunded and academically marginalized. Patients dying of cancers that metabolic intervention might address are paying the price for institutional orthodoxy.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Suppressed Hormonal Framework That Upends Mainstream Medicine
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov lays out a coherent, evidence-backed framework connecting estrogen dominance, histamine overload, serotonin excess, and endotoxemia — a metabolic and hormonal model that explains chronic disease patterns mainstream medicine treats symptomatically with drugs. This bioenergetic framework, rooted in the work of Ray Peat, has been systematically excluded from medical education, clinical guidelines, and research funding despite accumulating mechanistic support. The suppression serves a pharmaceutical industry that profits from treating each symptom in isolation rather than addressing root hormonal and metabolic dysregulation.

articles.title: FDA Suppressed Breastfeeding, Enabled Formula Monopoly — Then Triggered a National Infant Shortage

The agency that was supposed to protect infant nutrition instead created conditions for corporate formula dependency and then failed to ensure supply safety or continuity. Mothers and newborns paid the price while the agency protected industry relationships.

articles.title: FDA Rejected This Lymphoma Therapy Twice — Then Quietly Accepted the Same Study Design It Once Called Insufficient
articles.summary: After two rejections, the rare lymphoma cell therapy tabelecleucel has been resubmitted to the FDA using a single-arm study design the agency itself previously questioned — exposing a pattern of arbitrary, inconsistent evidentiary standards that have nothing to do with science and everything to do with institutional discretion. This inconsistency raises an unavoidable question: what determines FDA approval standards when the goalposts visibly move between applicants? Rare disease patients are caught in a regulatory system that cannot even apply its own rules consistently.

The mechanism — TIM-3-dependent macrophage repolarization — is novel, reproducible, and completely outside the pharmaceutical development pipeline because it cannot be patented and monetized like an Ozempic analog. This is exactly the kind of metabolic research that gets buried under the weight of GLP-1 hype.
